mediaWork.title: A False Report: A True Story of Rape in America
mediaWork.creatorName: T. Christian Miller and Ken Armstrong
mediaWork.focusOrTheme: Investigation of false rape accusations, victim credibility, police investigation methods
mediaWork.summaryNotes: The book follows two parallel narratives: Marie Adler's experience being disbelieved and charged with filing a false report after being raped, and the later investigation by two female detectives in Colorado who connected multiple rape cases and eventually identified Marc O'Leary as the serial rapist responsible.  While not a traditional wrongful conviction case, it highlights similar systemic issues such as skepticism toward certain types of witnesses, pressure to close cases quickly, and the devastating impact of being disbelieved by the justice system. The book was expanded from a Pulitzer Prize-winning ProPublica/Marshall Project article.
